## Example 1.5 {#ss1-example-1-5}

A sequence is defined by the conditions $a_1=1$ and $a_n=\dfrac{n-1}{n}a_{n-1}$.

Find the first five terms and conjecture a formula for the $n$th term of the sequence.

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 3 · Example 1.5 · Complete the working in your booklet.</p>

::: notes
The recursive relation applies for n≥2; the source omits that range, so explain it alongside the preserved question.

a_1=1; a_2=(1/2)×1=1/2; a_3=(2/3)×(1/2)=1/3; a_4=(3/4)×(1/3)=1/4; a_5=(4/5)×(1/4)=1/5. Conjecture a_n=1/n for positive integers n. A common error is to use only (n−1)/n and forget to multiply by the previous term. Conjecturing is sufficient; induction is not required.
:::
